title: Riftwatch — quick handoff & triage cheatsheet
content:
Quick handoff notes for the 0200–1000 PST shift (Riftwatch). Mostly a scratchpad — assume things will change.

Summary / state at handoff:
- Low-severity: CPU < 70% cluster-wide; memory GC spikes on serving-runtime pods occasionally around 03:30 (investigating).
- Ongoing: intermittent 503s on /v1/generate from hosted-api in us-west-2 during bursts (~5–10 min windows). Rate-limiter downstream seems healthy.
- Recent change: rolled model rwd-v2-small -> rwd-v2-small-quant on canary at 2026-02-27 22:10; canary metrics look OK but tail latency bumped +12% in the 95th pct.

Incidents & timeline (short):
- 2026-02-28 01:12 — spike of 503s for 8 min; cause traced to a single serving node OOM (kubelet evicted kernel). Node recovered after GCE autoscaler restart.
  - Action taken: evacuated pods, cordoned node, flagged for follow-up (node: gke-runt-3c-7p).
  - Jira: OPS-789 (linked).
- 2026-02-28 03:37 — brief GC pause on runtime-pod s-rt-12, increased tokenization latency; restarted pod (kubectl rollout restart deploy/serving-runtime-usw2).

Open tasks (please pick up if you have capacity):
- Follow up on node repro (ops-789) — check kernel logs, vm.max_map_count, containerd version mismatch. Tagged Diego to take a deeper look.
- Watch canary of v2-small-quant for another 12h; if 95th pct tail > +10% vs baseline, rollback to v2-small and open a model-performance investigation.
- Verify cache backfill job tomorrow @ 05:00 PST (cron job id: cache-prefill-usw2). Last run skipped due to transient API 401 on credentials rotation — Priya has the creds fix in infra PR #432.

Temporary runbook / quick play actions (for the next 4–6 hours):
1) If you see widespread 503s on /v1/generate (>1m error rate >1%), first check the per-route dashboard: https://observability.redwood/api/dashboards/route-generate-usw2
   - Cmds: kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=serving-runtime -o wide
   - Look for pods in CrashLoopBackOff, OOMKilled, or NodeNotReady.
2) If a single node is OOMing repeatedly: cordon + drain, then scale up a new node pool temporarily (policy: surge scaling):
   - kubectl cordon <node-name>
   - kubectl drain <node-name> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
   - gcloud compute instance-groups managed resize <mig-name> --size=<current+2> (ask infra if you're not sure about the MIG name)
3) If 95th-latency on canary model > 10% above baseline for > 30 minutes: rollback canary:
   - kubectl -n prod set image deploy/canary-serving model=rwd-v2-small:stable
   - verify endpoints via curl against canary endpoint (/internal/canary/health) and check perf dashboard.
4) Short-term cache flush (only if you understand KV cache semantics):
   - curl -X POST $CACHE_ADMIN_URL/flush?prefix=token_prefix
   - Note: flushing increases CPU for ~10–20m as requests rebuild KV. Avoid during traffic spikes.
5) If tokenization stalls (seen as sudden rise in TTFB before model exec): restart tokenizer-worker on the node: systemctl restart tokenizer-worker (only on affected pod node after cordon).

Useful commands (copy-paste economy):
- kubectl -n prod logs deploy/serving-runtime --tail=200 | sed -n '1,200p'
- kubectl -n prod get hpa --watch
- kubectl -n infra get jobs | grep cache-prefill && kubectl -n infra logs job/cache-prefill-<id>
- gcloud compute ssh <node> --zone=us-west2-b --command='sudo journalctl -u kubelet -n 200'

Dashboards & logs to check (bookmarks):
- Route perf: https://observability.redwood/api/dashboards/route-generate-usw2
- Node/instance health: https://observability.redwood/gce-nodes
- Serving runtime traces (sampled): https://traces.redwood/serving-runtime
- Auth/credentials vault events: https://vault.redwood/events (search for "rotation")

Escalation contacts (pager order):
- First: Diego Alvarez (pager: pager+diego@pagerduty) — infra/kernel/node issues
- Second: Priya Nair (pager) — infra CI/credentials, deployments
- Third: On-call engineering manager: Raj Patel — policy/approval for scaling beyond reserved quota
- SRE Rotations: #sre-oncall (Slack) — mute if incident is contained and ping later

Nightnotes / things I noticed (notes to self):
- The OOM on gke-runt-3c-7p looked like a host-level oom (not container-limited). Check node taints/swap settings.
- Canary traffic profile skewed: more long-context tests than baseline; might be a test job leaking longer prompts into canary. Verify upstream test job IDs in logs (search for job: perf-e2e-long-ctx).
- cache-prefill cron needs resilient retries; current job exits on first HTTP 401 — add 3 retries with exponential backoff. (PR queued: infra#432).

Followups for next weekday shift:
- Add a small probe that triggers tokenization warmup after deploys (low cost, 5 requests/sec for 2 min).
- Schedule a deeper node-profiling run for gke-runt-3c-7p with perf tool (coordinate with infra).
- If rollback happens, open a model-eval ticket to run the small-quant vs baseline test-suite across longer contexts.

Loose TODOs (non-blocking):
- Rework canary routing policy to split by request size (short vs long contexts) — product input needed.
- Draft a short runbook for tokenizer restarts (safe steps + checks).

Questions for you (next oncall) — things to clarify quickly:
- Did you see any scheduled jobs run around 00:45–01:10? Might correlate with the spike.
- If you decide to drain node gke-runt-3c-7p, please update OPS-789 with the drain time and attach node logs.

Signoff:
- Leaving the primary channel monitored (I will check in at 07:00 PST). Ping me on Slack if you need pairing (Maya Chen).

-- scratch/notes end --

(If you're the person taking this, feel free to tidy or delete this doc when you consolidate the official handoff.)
